Android may stop the governor when the phone idles. Turn battery optimization off for CoreGovernor so it can stay alive in the background.
Done. Battery optimization is now off for CoreGovernor.
The root method did not work, so Android\'s own prompt is opening. Choose Allow.
Some phone brands also have their own Autostart or Background settings. If the governor still stops, check them in Open app settings.
While a selected app (Apps tab > Afterburn list) is in front and the conditions below are met, the power-throttle cap is temporarily bypassed. Thermal throttling always stays in charge.
Give one app its own strength. Default follows the setting above.
Only boost when the temperature is at least this many degrees below your thermal throttle start (%1$s °C). More headroom means a stronger boost.
3 to 8 °C. When the battery is low this margin is raised by 2 °C, so the two conditions decide together.
Boost less when the battery is below the threshold (discharging). Close to empty there is no boost. Charging ignores this condition.
Below this level the boost is reduced.
Boost less when the battery voltage drops a lot under load (learned from the battery\'s own behaviour). Protects a weak or cold cell. Stops the boost at about 400 mV of sag.
Briefly shows a floating pill at the top when Afterburn engages for a selected app (requires Display over other apps permission).
Grant superuser (su) in Magisk / KernelSU / APatch, then tap refresh above.
Start governor to stream live telemetry history
No data yet. Start the governor on the Monitor tab. Graphs fill in at one point per second.
Nothing saved yet. A session is recorded while a game from the Apps tab is in the foreground, and saved once it lasts at least 20 seconds. The newest 40 are kept.

FPS per watt = FPS shown by the app divided by battery power draw. Work per watt = (CPU cluster frequency × cores × load + GPU frequency × load), in busy GHz, divided by power. Work is an estimate, not a benchmark, so compare it only on this phone. Higher is more efficient. Ratios use a 5-second average and are blank while power is below 0.3 W or there is no FPS.
This will permanently remove all saved sessions and cannot be undone.
drag to inspect • double-tap to clear
Each line has its own scale: %1$s
This clears all collected frequency power estimates and per-app scenarios. Re-learning takes a few hours of normal and gaming use.
This clears the learned discharge/charge capacity segments and restarts battery capacity estimation from scratch.
Enter your battery\'s rated design capacity in mAh, or leave 0 / empty for auto-detection from sysfs.
Learning paused: charging (settled discharging samples only)
Passively learns device power vs frequency and load in the background while discharging. Takes hours of normal + game use for high confidence.
Uses learned power/perf curves to pick lower-energy frequencies within your allowed min/max and thermal/power caps once confident.
Standard scaling is kept for any frequency bucket below this confidence threshold.
Occasional safe adjacent-step probes while Efficiency governor is active.
Hardware components not discovered yet. Start the governor or run discovery on Monitor to inspect learned power curves.
Collecting data: needs about %1$d%% uninterrupted %2$s (≥3 min) for initial estimate%3$s.

Uses battery-side net current (screen, idle, and charger/load balance included).
Gauge second opinion: ~%1$d mAh (%2$d mAh left at %3$s)
Session: Out %1$s Wh (%2$s mAh) • In %3$s Wh (%4$s mAh)
Lifetime: Out %1$s Wh (%2$s mAh) • In %3$s Wh (%4$s mAh)
Tracks charge/discharge energy across uninterrupted percent steps (~8%+ and 3+ min) to estimate real battery health.
Calibrated: full charge %1$d mV%2$s, discharge curve learned
Calibrating: keep charging to 100% until it stops taking power
Calibrating: keep discharging, do not plug in
Charge calibrated (%1$d mV). Next: one unplugged discharge from 95%% to empty
Discharge calibrated. Next: one undisturbed charge to 100%
Not calibrated: one undisturbed charge to 100% and one unplugged discharge from 95% to empty teaches the battery type
Learns what each app asks of every CPU cluster and the GPU. Learning only runs while this is on and needs hours of use. Thermal, caps, pins and Game mode always win.
No data yet - use your apps normally.
Deletes everything learned for this app. It will start learning again from shared knowledge.

Drops the panel to the lowest rate when idle and boosts on touch. Your original refresh-rate settings are saved and restored when you turn this off or stop the service. Needs root; use Test switch first.
Deletes all recorded screen-off periods and daily totals.
Measures battery drain, deep sleep and what keeps the phone awake while the screen is off (3 min or longer, not charging). Needs the service running.
No data yet. Leave the screen off for a few minutes (unplugged) and check back.
Very high drain - something is keeping the phone awake
Standby estimate: ~%1$s h from full to empty
Deep sleep is low: the CPU is being woken or held awake for a large part of the off time. Check the wake sources below.
Kernel wake sources (time active while off)
No app wakelocks seen while the screen was off.
Normal mode uses moderate max clocks for cool daily usage.
Game mode keeps clocks pinned closer to your chosen ceiling until throttling starts.
Grant root access and tap Discover Hardware to configure per-cluster frequencies.
Lowest clock this cluster is allowed to drop to in %1$s mode.
Highest clock allowed before thermal/power caps in %1$s mode.
Lowest GPU OPP position allowed in %1$s mode.
Highest GPU OPP position pinned via /proc/gpufreqv2/fix_target_opp_index.
How often the loop reads /proc/stat, GPU load, thermals, and updates clocks (100–250 ms recommended).

When the phone is idle and calm for a couple of seconds, the loop checks a little less often (up to about 350 ms) to save battery and CPU. It goes back to your Poll Interval the instant you touch the screen, open a game or app, load rises, or throttling starts. Turn off to always poll at the Poll Interval.
Hard minimum ceiling percentage so thermal or power throttling can never stall the phone.
Adds extra load margin before grading CPU frequencies to avoid sluggishness on sudden demand.
Higher values jump CPU clocks upward fast when load spikes so frames never stutter.
Lower values hold higher CPU clocks briefly after load drops; keep very low in Games mode.
Raises effective GED GPU utilization before picking a position in the sorted OPP table.
Controls how aggressively GPU OPP index climbs on shader/render load spikes.
Controls how slowly GPU OPP index steps down after GPU load drops.
Briefly boosts to top allowed clock on app switch or sudden load spike, then settles back.
Length of the launch burst window (up to 2000 ms) before settling to normal scaling.
Single-poll CPU load jump that triggers a burst even within the same app.
Grades each cluster by its busiest core instead of the cluster average, so one pegged core can reach the top clock. Turn off for the old averaged behavior.
Launches CoreGovernor foreground service automatically after Android finishes booting.

If the governor was running when the phone restarted, it starts again by itself as soon as Android finishes booting, even with Start Automatically off. Pressing Stop turns this off until you start it again.
Boot guard skipped the last automatic start because the governor kept stopping right after boot. Start it by hand; this note clears after a stable run.
Pins the memory clock to its highest step. Can reduce stutter, but uses more battery and runs warmer. Released when the screen is off.
Pin only while a game is in the foreground.
Pins all CPU and GPU clocks to minimum while the screen is off. Stops all frequency changes during sleep.
Wait time after the screen turns off before pinning clocks to minimum.
Keep normal while music is playing
Skips sleep saving while active audio playback is detected.
Skips sleep saving while the device is plugged into a charger.
Displays a floating CPU, GPU, thermal, and power monitor over other apps.
Lets touches pass through the overlay. Use the notification action to unlock.
Shows the overlay only when Game mode is active.
Fades the whole overlay, text included, from 30% to 100%.
Fades only the dark background behind the numbers, from 0% (fully see-through) to 100%. The text stays fully readable.
Fine: sliders zoomed to ±10 pts around current value.
Enable Fine to zoom sliders, or use − / + to step.
Scales the compact overlay pill (%1$d%%–%2$d%% on this screen).
Scales the expanded overlay card (%1$d%%–%2$d%% on this screen).
Positions the overlay horizontally along available screen width.
Positions the overlay vertically along available screen height.
Scales this overlay on its own (%1$d%%–%2$d%% on this screen).
Size of the labels and values in this style. The overlay gets wider or taller with it, and the Size slider limit adjusts so it still fits the screen.
Background of this overlay only. The main background opacity slider sets all three, then adjust here.
CPU Policies: %1$d | GPU OPPs: %2$d | Thermal Sensors: %3$d
Gradually lowers CPU and GPU max frequency caps as the chosen thermal sensor heats up.
Selects whether battery, SoC, or CPU thermal zone drives the thermal curve.
Temperature where cap reduction begins smoothly from 100%.
Temperature where thermal throttling reaches its full configured reduction.
Maximum percentage cut applied to CPU clusters at full-strength temperature.
Maximum percentage cut applied to GPU frequency range at full-strength temperature.
Gentle delays heavy cuts until hot; Aggressive trims clocks early near start temp.
Controls how quickly the thermal cap adapts to temperature changes.
Temperature must cool down by this margin before the thermal cap relaxes.
Lowers throttle start temp slightly while charging or plugged in to account for charger heat.
Starts thermal throttling at %1$s °C when charging/plugged.
Enable charging-aware thermal above to offset start temperature when plugged in.
Gently steps down clock caps when sustained wattage stays above your budget to prevent heat buildup.

Average model confidence needed before the smooth limit alternates between two steps. Lower = it kicks in sooner (less exact), higher = it waits for a better-trained model. The log shows the current average when it is not active.

Shortest time the smooth limit stays on one of its two frequency steps. Shorter = finer, steadier average power but more frequency writes through the root shell. 50 ms is the behaviour before 4.0.9; the log line WriteLat shows how long writes really take.

Tries shorter slices one CPU cluster at a time, only during long steady game sessions under the power limit. A shorter slice is kept only while overshoot or FPS steadiness gets better and nothing gets worse; otherwise it goes back to the last good slice. Never below 30 ms. Each change is logged as SmoothSlice. The slider is the starting point.

When the kernel or vendor code changes the frequency limits behind the smooth limit, write the value again (at most every 0.4 s per cluster, never while a temperature cap is active). Off = the override stays until the next switch. The log shows how many were fixed (CpuDrift).

Instead of parking on one frequency step, switch quickly between two neighbouring steps so the average power lands on the limit. A separate fast timer does the switching, so it works with any normal poll interval. Also smooths thermal caps (no watt-based trim there). Needs a confident power model; otherwise the normal limit is used. See the log (SmoothLimit).
When power is over the limit, throttle the heavier consumer (CPU or GPU, and the busiest CPU cluster) more.
Average device wattage threshold above which the sustain timer begins counting.
How long draw must stay above the watt limit before reducing the cap by one step.
Small percentage cut applied per step while power remains over budget.
Gradual cap recovery per cycle once wattage drops safely below the budget.
Smooths brief battery current spikes over N poll cycles before comparing against limit.
Match your kernel\'s sysfs unit scale and discharge sign convention so live watts read accurately.
Keeps the chosen sensors running at a fast, fixed rate for every app, so a slow gyroscope responds quicker. Runs while the governor is running. No root needed.
Max asks the sensor for its fastest rate. Rates above 200 Hz need the high-sampling-rate permission, which the app declares.
No supported motion sensors found on this device.
Pause while the screen is off
Releases the sensors when the screen turns off and pins them again when it turns on. Saves battery.
Only pin while in a game
Pins the sensors only while a game is detected and running (Game mode), and releases them otherwise. Cuts idle power use.
Waiting for a game. Sensors are not pinned right now.
Waiting: starts when the governor starts.
Paused (screen off) or no sensor could be registered. See the log.
Freezes the live highlight and raw status card until turned off or refreshed.
Starts this screen paused every time you open the app, so you do not have to switch it on each time. The Refresh button still takes a fresh reading.
No GPU OPP entries parsed yet. Ensure root is granted and refresh.
Tap Refresh or start CoreGovernor to inspect live /proc/gpufreqv2/gpufreq_status output.
Use the phone with the governor running. About 30 minutes of unplugged use are needed (%1$s so far).
Charging time is not counted. Compare phones only on similar usage. On one phone, a higher score after a settings change means that setting suits your usage better.

Sorted by CPU use (% of one core). Culprits are apps that kept using a lot of CPU in the background for about 30 seconds. Stopping an app is done with root, and it may start again by itself. Core system processes are protected and cannot be stopped.
It will be force-stopped with root. It may start again by itself, and unsaved data in it is lost.
The collected totals are cleared and the rating starts again from zero.
Could not read the process list. Root access is needed.
Stopped %1$s. It may start again by itself.
Fast foreground app events switch between Normal and Game modes.
Grant Usage Access for instant app-switch detection, or rely on root dumpsys window fallback.

Tick the games that switch the governor into Game mode.
Search installed apps or package name…
Only one refresh rate is supported - feature unavailable.
Learns each game\'s normal FPS. When FPS dips well below normal, finds which background app is using CPU and reports or stops it.
Triggers when FPS drops below this percentage of the game\'s learned normal FPS.
Minimum average CPU load (of one core) required to blame another app.
Apps on your whitelist are never blamed or stopped.

resources.string: Charge data trust: %1$d%% (fast charging counts less toward capacity)
While the screen is off and the phone is charging, stops background apps that wake the CPU and heat the phone. Needs root.
Also stops every installed user app that is not on the whitelist, every minute. Your launcher, keyboard and phone are always kept.
Apps that must keep running, like messengers or alarms.
Apps and system processes to stop every time the screen is off while charging.
Detects the power button while the screen is off and boosts clocks to maximum straight away, so unlocking is quicker.
Pins matched threads of the foreground game to selected CPU cores using taskset -p at most once every 2 seconds while in Game mode.
Fallback when no custom mappings exist: conservatively assigns Main/Render threads to Big (6-7) and Worker threads to Mid (3-5).
Pin game threads to specific CPU cores via taskset during Game mode.
Root access is unavailable. Grant superuser access to inspect /proc/[pid]/task and apply taskset affinity.
No configured game is currently in the foreground. Add games in the Apps tab and launch one to inspect live threads.
Foreground game detected, but no active process PID is available yet. Tap Refresh once the game finishes starting.
No readable threads found under /proc/%1$d/task. The process may have exited or denied /comm reads.
Select at least one available CPU core
No custom mappings saved. Auto-classification fallback is enabled for Main, Render, and Worker threads.
No custom thread mappings configured yet.
Device reports %1$d CPUs (0–%2$d available); higher cores disabled.
CoreGovernor is in front; %1$s is still running in the background (PID %2$d). Showing refreshed live threads.
Game is not currently active or live threads are unavailable. Showing saved thread history.
Observed thread names are persisted per game so you can inspect and map threads even when the game is no longer in the foreground. Taskset only applies to currently live TIDs.
No stored thread history yet. Launch or refresh a configured game to capture its threads.
Remove all saved thread observations for %1$s? Your saved CPU mappings will be kept.
Remove all saved thread observations across all games? Your saved CPU mappings will be kept.
Select 2 to 4 sessions to compare (%1$d selected).
Settings changed mid-session (%1$d time(s)). Shown snapshot is from session start.
All recorded settings matched across these sessions.
Session %1$s: %2$s FPS avg, %3$s, %4$s vs A. Changes: %5$s
At least one session included charging (power comparison may be skewed).
Settings changed mid-session in at least one run.
Settings were not recorded for at least one session.
At least one session has fewer than 20 samples.
Analyzed %1$d recorded session(s) for this game.
Record at least 2 sessions with varying settings to rank tweak impact.
Custom per-game overrides are active in Game mode.
Runs conservative single-change trials between game sessions using your saved performance score.
No trials yet. Play a normal unplugged session to capture the baseline.
Locked tweaks are never modified by Auto-Tune.
Ignored: phone was charging during the session.
Ignored: session shorter than minimum valid length.
Improved composite score above margin; change kept.
Did not beat best score by margin; reverted.
